q: 1. Gantt chart indicates
options: balance of work to be done
comparison of actual progress with the scheduled progress
explain: The primary purpose of a Gantt (Bar) chart is to provide a visual comparison between the actual progress of tasks and the original schedule.

q: 2. Henry Gnatt developed the bar chart technique in
explain: Henry Gantt developed his namesake bar chart technique around 1900 AD to help supervisors see whether they were on schedule.

q: 3. The bar chart is also known as
explain: Bar charts were developed by Henry Gantt and are universally known as Gantt charts.

q: 4. Henry Gantt developed the bar chart technique in
explain: Henry Gantt devised his historical system of project progress charts around 1900–1915.

q: 5. Critical path method is an effective and powerful method of assessing
options: What tasks must be carried out
Where parallel activities can be performed
The shortest time in which you can complete a project
explain: CPM identifies required tasks, parallel activity opportunities, and the minimum project duration - covering all listed aspects.

q: 6. An example for a parallel activity is
options: completing ground floor and starting first floor
wall and carpentry work of doors and windows
completion of flooring and initiating white washing
digging of a well and of septic tank
explain: Parallel activities can happen simultaneously; wall construction and carpentry can often proceed at the same time in different sections.

q: 7. The use of bar chart is very popular in construction department because
options: it is very simple to prepare and interpret
each item of work or activity is shown separately
modification to the chart, if required, can be carried out easily
explain: Bar charts are simple, show each activity separately and are easy to modify.

q: 8. Free float is mainly used to
options: identify the activities which can be delayed without affecting the total float of preceeding activity
identify the activities, which can be delayed without affecting the total float of succeeding activity
identify the activities which can be delayed without affecting the total float of either the preceeding or succeeding activities
explain: Free float is the amount of time an activity can be delayed without affecting the earliest start time of any immediately following (succeeding) activities.

q: 9. On a bar chart the various activities of a project are shown by
explain: Each activity is a horizontal bar drawn against the time scale.

q: 10. The weakness in bar chart is
options: uncertainty in duration for various activities
the sequence of activities is not very clear
explain: Bar charts do not show interdependencies, uncertainty or clear sequence.

q: 11. Latest start of activity is always
options: less than or equal to latest event time of preceeding node
more than or equal to latest events time of preceeding node
equal to latest event time of preceeding node
explain: The latest an activity can start must be at or after the latest time its preceding event (node) can occur.

q: 12. The independent float affects only
explain: By definition, independent float is the time by which an activity can be delayed without affecting any other activity in the network.

q: 13. The probability factor Z in PERT is given by
options: (scheduled time – earliest expected time) / standard deviation
(latest allowable time – scheduled time) / standard deviation
explain: Z = (TS – TE)/σ, where TS is the scheduled time and TE the earliest expected time.

q: 14. A drawback of the bar chart is that
options: it is difficult to judge whether an activity is completed or not
all the activities represented are independent of each other
sequence of activities is not clearly defined
it is not possible to judge whether the activity is ahead or behind schedule
explain: Bar charts do not show the logical sequence or interdependence of activities.

q: 15. For completion of a project, the CPM of the network represents
explain: The Critical Path Method identifies the minimum time required to complete the entire project based on the sequence of dependent tasks.

q: 16. Expected project duration generally follows
explain: Per the answer key, a. The project duration is a sum of many activity times, so by the central limit theorem it is taken as normal. Activity times follow the beta curve.

q: 17. Bar chart is suitable for
explain: Bar charts are simple and versatile, suitable for representing schedules of projects of all sizes - major and minor alike.

q: 18. The first method invented for planning projects, was
explain: The bar chart (Gantt chart) method, invented in the late 1800s, was the earliest project planning tool, preceding milestone charts, CPM, and PERT.

q: 19. CPM is
explain: CPM is activity oriented.

q: 20. Which of the following statements is true?
options: PERT is activity oriented and adopts deterministic approach
CPM is event oriented and adopts probabilistic approach
CPM is activity oriented and adopts probabilistic approach
PERT is event oriented and adopts probabilistic approach
explain: PERT is event oriented and probabilistic. CPM is activity oriented and deterministic.

q: 21. PERT technique of network analysis is useful for
explain: PERT is ideally suited for Research and Development projects where the duration of activities is uncertain and has not been performed before.

q: 22. The critical activity has
explain: By definition, a critical activity has zero total float, since any delay would push back the overall project completion.

q: 23. If the optimistic time, most likely time and pessimistic time for activity A are 4, 6 and 8 respectively and for activity B are 5, 5.5 and 9 respectively, then
options: expected time of activity A is greater than the expected time of activity B
expected time of activity B is greater than the expected time of activity A
expected time of both activities A and B are same
explain: tE(A) = (4+24+8)/6 = 6 and tE(B) = (5+22+9)/6 = 6, so they are equal.

q: 24. The time which result in the least possible construction cost of an activity, is known
explain: (May be wrong )As per book Normal time is the duration at which the activity's direct cost is minimum (most economical execution pace).

q: 25. PERT is
options: used for research and development projects
based on three time estimates for activities linking up two events
explain: PERT is event-oriented, commonly used for R&D projects with uncertain durations, and relies on three time estimates linking events - all statements are true.

q: 26. The probability of completion of any activity within its expected time in PERT is
explain: The expected time ($t_e$) in a normal distribution represents the 50% probability mark (the mean).

q: 27. In CPM analysis,
explain: CPM emphasizes activities, assumes deterministic (certain) durations, and represents activities as arrows - all statements are correct.

q: 28. Variance is
options: Sum of time duration for various job / number of jobs
difference between the time under consideration and mean time
square root of mean of squared deviation
explain: Variance is defined statistically as the mean of squared deviations[cite: 1].

q: 29. All the following are valid for CPM except
options: the beginning and end of an activity is denoted by nodes
explain: CPM assumes deterministic, certain activity durations; allowing uncertainties is NOT valid for CPM (that characteristic belongs to PERT).

q: 30. The occurrence of the completion of an activity is called its
explain: The completion event is the head event, at the arrowhead.

q: 31. For a curve, larger the variance
explain: Variance is a measure of spread; a higher variance means the actual time could deviate significantly from the mean, increasing uncertainty.

q: 32. If an activity has its optimistic, most likely and pessimistic time are 2, 4 & 6 respectively, then its expected time and variance are respectively
33. Positive slack indicates
explain: Positive slack means there is extra time available, implying the project or event is ahead of its required deadline.

q: 34. In PERT technique, completion of an activity is called
explain: The completion of an activity is the head event (arrowhead end).

q: 35. If the completion time for a particular project is 6 weeks and its expected time is 8 weeks, then the slack time for the project is
explain: Slack time is calculated as (Scheduled Time - Expected Time). Here, 6 weeks - 8 weeks = -2 weeks. Negative slack indicates the project is behind schedule.

q: 36. If D is the duration, ES and EF are the earliest start and earliest finish time, LS and LF are latest start and latest finish time, then following relation holds good
explain: In network analysis, finish times are the start times plus duration, and start times are finish times minus duration. All these formulas correctly represent the relationships between activity timings.

q: 37. The expected project duration in CPM follow
explain: While individual activities in PERT follow a Beta distribution, the total project duration (due to the Central Limit Theorem) is assumed to follow a Normal Distribution.

q: 38. Which of the following denotes a dummy activity P?
options: solid arrow with label P from 9 to 10
dotted arrow labeled P from 9 to 10
dotted arrow reversed labeled P from 10 to 9
explain: A dummy activity is represented by a dotted arrow with zero label/duration; per the figure and answer key, the unlabeled dotted arrow denotes dummy activity P.

q: 39. Free float for any activity is defined as the difference between
options: its earliest finish time and earliest start time for its successor activity
Its latest start time and earliest start time
its latest finish time and earliest start time for successor activity
its earliest finish time and latest start time for its successor activity
explain: Free float = earliest start of the successor – earliest finish of the activity.

q: 40. If the height of the frequency-distribution underneath is equal to unity, then curve is known as
explain: A standard normal distribution curve is defined such that the total area underneath the curve is equal to unity (1.0).

q: 41. The estimated time required to complete an activity is known as
explain: That is the activity duration.

q: 42. Critical path method
options: makes better and detailed planning possible
provides a standard method for communication project plans, schedules time and cost performance
explain: All three are CPM benefits.

q: 43. The constraint in case of resource smoothing operation would be
explain: Resource smoothing aims to even out resource usage without changing the project completion date, making time the primary constraint.

q: 44. Free float is the
explain: Free float is the part of positive total float that can be used without affecting successors.

q: 45. Which is/are features of PERT/CPM?
options: An estimate of how long a project will take.
A graphical display of project activities.
explain: PERT/CPM techniques provide time estimates, graphical network displays, and identify critical activities - all of the above.

q: 46. Slack is
options: difference of lastest allowable time and earliest expected time
earliest expected time - lastest allowable time
explain: Slack = latest allowable time – earliest expected time.

q: 47. Pick up the correct statement from the following
options: in a network activities are represented by arrows and events are circled
events into which a number of activities enter and from which one or several activities emerge are called the merge nodes
events into which one or several activities enter and from which a number of emerging activities are generated are called burst nodes
explain: All three statements are correct, so d.

q: 48. Interfering float is the difference between
explain: Interfering float = total float – free float.

q: 49. The process of incorporating changes and rescheduling or replanning is called
explain: Updating is the process of incorporating changes and rescheduling/replanning the project based on actual progress.

When events stick to their schedule
